terminal.description: The route board runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell is in your workspace if you want to look around.

tasks.title: Narrow the list as you type
tasks.description:
Make the search box `#search` work while someone types:

- in `src/main.js`, draw the board again on every `input` event of `#search` (the check fires `input` only, the event every keystroke sends)
- in `src/filter.js`, `matches(route, query, band)` keeps a route when its name contains `query`, ignoring upper and lower case and any spaces around `query`
- an empty search keeps every route, in the original order

Ticks stay as they are while routes are searched out of view, and `#tick-count` keeps counting every route.
nextSteps: Read `render()` in `main.js`: it already asks `matches` about every route.
Add an `input` listener on `#search` that calls `render`.
In `matches`, compare the route name with the query in one letter case.
Type in the box in the Browser panel and watch the list shrink.
hints: Two pieces are missing: nothing redraws the board when the text changes, and `matches` says yes to everything.
The `change` event of a text box fires only when it loses focus. `input` fires on every keystroke.
Trim the query and lower-case both strings, then use `includes`. An empty string is included in every name, which is exactly what an empty search needs.

tasks.title: Filter by grade
tasks.description:
Make the grade select `#grade-filter` work too. Its values are `''` (any grade), `'easy'`, `'mid'` and `'hard'`, the same bands as the badges.

- draw the board again when its value changes
- `matches` keeps a route only when its band is the chosen one, or when the value is `''`
- the search and the grade apply together, so a route has to pass both
nextSteps: In `filter.js`, import the function from `board.js` that turns a grade into a band.
Return false early when the name does not match, then decide on the band.
Try a search and a grade together in the Browser panel.
hints: You already wrote the grade to band rule for the badges. Reuse it instead of writing it again.
Export it from `board.js` if it is not exported, and import it with a relative path ending in `.js`.
The band test is: the band is empty, or the route's band equals it. Combine it with the name test using `&&` or an early return.

tasks.title: Say when nothing matches
tasks.description:
When the filters leave no route on the board, show the `

` line, which starts hidden in `index.html`. - routes exist but none match: `#no-match` visible, `#board-empty` hidden - some routes match: `#no-match` hidden - no routes at all: `#board-empty` visible, `#no-match` hidden
nextSteps: Use the number of routes and the number shown to decide.
Search for something silly in the Browser panel to see the line.
Clear the search and check that it goes away.
hints: Two different empty boards need two different sentences. What tells them apart?
`routes` is everything on the wall and `shown` is what passed the filters. You need both.
The line is hidden when there are no routes at all, or when at least one route is shown.
